title: Diagonal Traverse Problem

content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: Starting at the top-left, traverse each diagonal alternately upward-right and downward-left.
The traversal changes direction whenever it reaches a matrix boundary.

content.problemStatement:
With an `m x n` matrix `mat`, output *an array of all the elements of the array in a diagonal order*.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2021/04/10/diag1-grid.jpg)

```
Input: mat = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
Output: [1,2,4,7,5,3,6,8,9]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: mat = [[1,2],[3,4]]
Output: [1,2,3,4]
```

**Constraints:**

* `m == mat.length`
* `n == mat[i].length`
* `1 <= m, n <= 10^4`
* `1 <= m * n <= 10^4`
* `-10^5 <= mat[i][j] <= 10^5`

solution.approach: Traverse the matrix one diagonal at a time. Maintain the current cell and alternate between moving up-right and down-left. When a boundary is reached, move to the next diagonal's starting cell and reverse direction. Every cell is visited exactly once.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(m * n) including the returned result; O(1) auxiliary space excluding the output.

bruteForce.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(m * n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Group cells by the diagonal index r + c, collect each diagonal, and reverse every even-indexed diagonal before concatenating the results. This is correct but uses additional storage for diagonal groups.

better.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding the output.
better.description: Use a single output array and simulate movement between cells while checking the four boundary conditions. This removes the need to store diagonal groups.

optimal.complexity: O(m * n) time and O(1) auxiliary space excluding the returned O(m * n) output.
optimal.description: Start at (0,0) and alternate up-right and down-left. At each boundary, advance to the next diagonal's entry point and reverse direction. Because exactly one matrix cell is appended per iteration, all m*n cells are visited exactly once without revisiting or sorting.

hints: Notice that cells on the same diagonal have the same value of r + c.
The required order alternates direction on consecutive diagonals.
Track one (row, column) position and change direction only when a matrix boundary is reached.
Be careful at corners: the next cell after a boundary belongs to the next diagonal, not the current one.
followUps: Can you implement the traversal without storing any intermediate diagonal lists?
How would the approach change if the matrix were streamed row by row instead of stored in memory?
Can you derive the output order directly from the diagonal index r + c?
learningObjectives: Simulate a two-direction matrix traversal with precise boundary handling.
Recognize diagonal structure using the invariant r + c.
Design an O(m*n) traversal that visits every matrix element exactly once.
Distinguish output storage from auxiliary working space.
